details:
- CVE-2026-53793: confine a daemon module whose path carries a "/./" inner
  boundary marker to the inner module root rather than only to the kernel
  chroot, by widening the single predicate every confined wrapper, the secure
  symlink handling and the directory scan test, so a symlink inside the module
  can no longer reach a sibling that is inside the chroot but outside the
  module; also sanitize the peer-supplied basis name on the client
- CVE-2026-70454: require CA verification for the gnutls and stunnel backends
  of the rsync-ssl helper and bind the server certificate to the requested
  host, so an on-path attacker can no longer present a certificate valid for
  another name; validate the hostname before it reaches the TLS client
- CVE-2026-70464: bound the peer-driven daemon handshake with an absolute
  deadline armed before any peer input is read, so an unauthenticated client
  can no longer hold a connection slot open past "max connections" by
  stalling the greeting or trickling arguments
- NOTE, behaviour change from the CVE-2026-70454 fix: rsync-ssl is now
  fail-closed for the backends that could not verify at all. With
  RSYNC_SSL_TYPE=gnutls or stunnel and RSYNC_SSL_CA_CERT unset the helper
  exits 1 instead of connecting without verification; set
  RSYNC_SSL_ALLOW_INSECURE_GNUTLS=1 or RSYNC_SSL_ALLOW_INSECURE_STUNNEL=1 to
  restore the old behaviour, and RSYNC_SSL_SKIP_HOSTNAME_CHECK=1 to keep CA
  verification without the hostname binding. The default openssl path is
  unchanged: it already verified, and still does
